title: 2011 Cranbrook Legal Studies Trial
notes: All 20 Section I questions checked against the PDF. The paper contains no answer key; answers are reasoned guesses. Questions 18-19 share the printed Jackson stimulus.

groups.stimulus: In the course of an armed robbery of a bank in which money is stolen, Jackson deliberately fires rounds into the walls and ceilings, causing significant damage.

questions.stem: Marco is on trial for sexual assault. With whom does the burden of proof lie?
questions.answerNote: The prosecution (the Crown) bears the burden of proof.

questions.stem: Paul is distracted while hunting. He bumps his arm and his rifle discharges killing his partner Tom. Which element of criminal liability is lacking?
Which of the following is a case of situational crime prevention?
Which of the following are rights of the accused in the NSW criminal justice system?

options.A: Security of person and rights to a lawyer
options.C: Rights to silence and right to a phone call
options.D: Rights to silence and right to a lawyer

questions.stem: Which of the following best protects the human rights of an Australian citizen?

options.B: The United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights

questions.stem: Which of the following could be considered preliminary crimes?
Monika has been sued for libel. What is the standard of proof in this case?

options.B: On the doctrine of natural law

questions.stem: The establishment of Police Youth liaison officers who work in the community is an example of which of the following?

options.A: Eliminating the incentive to commit crime

questions.stem: Which of the following allows individuals to vote freely for their elected representatives?

The United Nations General Assembly has criticised Australia over the suspension of the Racial Discrimination Act during the Northern Territory intervention. Which of the following allows Australia to ignore the UN?
Which of the following is included in the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights?
Which of the following groups is responsible for enforcing the criminal laws of the state?
Which of the following courts has no original jurisdiction?
What human rights are guaranteed under the Australian Constitution?

options.B: Freedom of religion and sexual preference
options.C: Freedom of religion and right of assembly
options.D: Freedom of religion and trial by jury

questions.stem: Which of the following best represents an essential element of a crime?

options.A: Must harm another person or their property
options.B: Must be legislated against by parliament
options.C: Must be proved on the balance of probabilities
options.D: Must be seen as harmful to the whole community

questions.stem: Josh has been charged with a high-range drink driving offence. He is 17. In which court will the matter be heard?
The idea that a child under the age of 10 is incapable of committing a crime is contained in which of the following principles?
The offence Jackson has committed can be described using which of the following terms?

options.B: Summary and offence against the person
options.D: Indictable and offence against the person

questions.stem: During sentencing the judge would consider the damage caused to be which of the following?
questions.answerNote: Extracted Q19 text duplicates Q18's stem and its options look like those of the damage-caused question, so the question is probably scrambled. Assuming it asks how damage is treated at sentencing: aggravating factor (C); D 'aggravating circumstance' is also plausible.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of Interpol?

options.A: To assist with the investigation of international crime
options.B: To assist the International Court of Justice in their pursuit of international crime
options.D: To act as the police force for the United Nations

questions.answerNote: Interpol facilitates international police cooperation and assists investigations; It does not prosecute international crimes or act as a UN police force.
